# EMS ProtoQuiz

> EMS ProtoQuiz turns EMS protocols into pharmacology quizzes, algorithm tests, and adaptive patient scenarios. Every answer is page-cited back to the source document, so providers study THEIR local protocols — not generic NREMT filler. Three products: a free iOS and Android app where an individual provider uploads their own protocol PDF; ProtoQuiz for Agencies, where an organization sends its protocol and ProtoQuiz builds and verifies the question bank for the whole department; and ProtoQuiz Research, a free, open reference built only from public agencies' protocols and not for sale: the United States EMS Protocol Census compares the medications, doses and routes in published US EMS protocols, and a second line of work, in progress, maps who answers the 911 call in each county and whether that service is public, private, hospital-based or a fire department. Built by a paramedic. Made by ProtoQuiz LLC.

## What it is

- A study app for EMTs and paramedics that quizzes you on your own agency, county, or state protocols.
- In the consumer app, an individual provider uploads a protocol PDF (formulary, treatment protocols, algorithms, procedures) and ProtoQuiz extracts it into quiz content. Agencies work differently — see the ProtoQuiz for Agencies section below.
- Quiz types: pharmacology (adult and pediatric doses, indications, contraindications, routes, mechanism, adverse effects), algorithm tests built from your protocol flowcharts, adaptive patient scenarios where the patient responds to your treatment decisions, and Learn Mode (spaced repetition on the meds you miss).
- Every answer links to the exact source page in your uploaded PDF. Nothing is generated outside that document. Users can edit any extraction and data themselves.
- NREMT prep is also included free: 1,700+ practice questions across EMT and Paramedic levels, per-option rationales, a readiness dashboard, and an adaptive exam simulator.
- Free tier: 3 per day of each generated feature, with no ads. Premium removes the limit.
- Available on iOS (iPhone/iPad) and Android. Both platforms ship two themes: Night Shift (dark) and Day Shift (light).

## Who it is for

- Paramedic and EMT students studying their local protocols (e.g., for field internship).
- New providers, or providers moving to a new agency/county/state who must learn an unfamiliar protocol set.
- Seasoned providers maintaining mastery of their current system.
- EMS agencies and training officers who want a protocol-study platform for their staff: see ProtoQuiz for Agencies (flat per-provider annual pricing, admin analytics, branded for the department).

## ProtoQuiz for Agencies (the B2B product) — works differently from the consumer app

- **Agencies do not upload anything, and neither do their crews.** The organization sends ProtoQuiz its protocol document, and the question bank is built from it as a one-time build for that agency. The agency is live 7 days after ProtoQuiz receives the protocol. There is no self-serve upload box handed to providers, so there is no set of unreviewed question banks from many different crew members.
- The bank is built and verified against the agency's own document before it is delivered. Doses, thresholds and criteria are checked against the page they came from, and ambiguous or contradictory source text is flagged for a human rather than resolved by guesswork.
- Every question carries a page citation to the agency's own protocol document, so a training officer can verify any question against the source page. A question that cannot be traced to a page does not ship.
- Questions are scoped by certification level using the agency's own scope-of-practice chart, including non-standard cert tiers — not a generic EMT/Paramedic split.
- Built around one short quiz per shift per provider, done between calls. Every attempt is scored and dated by name, and exports as a PDF training record for a medical director, chief, or state audit.
- A written clinical standard governs the content: a question earns its place only if getting it wrong on a call would change patient care. Phone numbers, appendix numbers, and policy boilerplate are explicitly excluded.
- Each agency gets its own subdomain (e.g. youragency.protoquiz.com), browser-based, no app install.
- ProtoQuiz is a training tool, not medical direction; the agency's local protocol and medical direction always govern. ProtoQuiz logs training time for the agency's CE record; the agency (its CE program or medical director) grants CE, and ProtoQuiz does not.

## Facts

- App Store rating: 4.9 out of 5 from 23 ratings; 2,526 App Store downloads (as of October 16, 2026).
- Usage (as of October 16, 2026): protocol sets uploaded from 43 US states plus international; 478 distinct protocol documents; about 117,000 protocol pages processed.
- Platform: iOS (iPhone/iPad) and Android.
- Maker: ProtoQuiz LLC (Colorado, USA), founded 2025. Founder is a working paramedic.
- Differentiator vs. NREMT-prep apps (e.g., Pocket Prep, Medic Tests): ProtoQuiz quizzes YOUR local/agency protocols from your own PDF with page-cited answers, rather than a fixed bank of generic national-registry questions. It also includes a free NREMT bank.
- Works with any full-length protocol document: statewide protocol sets, county SOPs, agency formularies, procedure manuals.
